label: no
controls_available: Six visible proxy turn buttons: NORTH, SOUTHWEST, and SOUTHEAST, each with counter-clockwise and clockwise actions.
SEAL certification button; certification is administrative and does not turn a disc.
RETRY is shown only after a failed certification and starts an action-triggered fresh challenge.
autonomous_processes: None: between agent actions, the current rose, legal-turn relation, and visible pieces remain unchanged.
grouped_control_modes: D=proxy_buttons: all six simplified disc-direction turn actions across all occurrences; each click requests one clockwise or counter-clockwise disc turn.
SEAL and conditional RETRY are administrative or reset controls, not outcome-affecting turn modes for the real-time witness.

clause_i.reason: For D=proxy_buttons, action history alone does not identify the current visible permutation. The generator has 90 depth-four frontier states, 78 of which pass its exact-config candidate filter; the shortest-path first-action sets over those candidates have an empty intersection, so a fixed q(I_t) cannot be optimal across the same initial action history.

clause_ii.reason: The current rose and reference rose are visible in the screenshot, and the six labelled proxy buttons identify the available actions. A bounded stationary visual policy with the endpoint frame (w=0 under the configured window) can map the visible permutation to a shortest-path turn; no temporal sequence is needed.

clause_iii.reason: For every Delta>0, with no new action the browser mechanic has no autonomous task-state transition: attempt() is called only by a button click and updates model.current synchronously. Therefore for 0<tau<Delta the task state and the value of every turn are unchanged, so neither strict Q loss inequality holds. Any 180-second deadline is clock-only and cannot supply this clause.

common_visible_process: There is no common visible autonomous process. The visible rose is static while the agent waits; a proxy-button click synchronously applies or refuses a turn, and SEAL/RETRY are action-triggered administrative or reset operations. Thus no Delta>0 and bounded window can satisfy all three clauses.

pre_run.reason: No generated instance has an autonomous outcome phase: every outcome-affecting rose turn must be supplied by an agent click, while certification is administrative. The pre-run category is therefore not applicable; in any event, the mathematical definition already fails at clause (iii), so an unresolved pre-run rate cannot change the No label.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 2 uses scramble_depth 4; simplified interaction is six labelled proxy buttons; the configured task clock has a 0 ms observation window and one frame.
The runtime also declares observation_window_ms=0, frames_per_observation=1, play_time_seconds=180, and synchronous execution.
Disc legality and sixth-turn state transitions are discrete functions; generation samples an exact-depth state and exports a static rose contract plus a shortest-path solution.
Simplified mode renders proxy buttons, and attempt() computes legality and updates the current state synchronously only when invoked by an action; refused turns leave the visible state unchanged.
Retry re-renders only after an agent click, submission is separate, and the six proxy buttons are wired directly to attempt() while SEAL is wired to submit().
The complete mechanic stylesheet supplies static layout and interaction styling; it defines no timer, animation, or physics behavior for the rose state.
The grader binds simplified events to proxy_buttons and replays the submitted discrete transcript, with completion determined by the final solved state rather than elapsed task time.
The exported verifier independently replays the same synchronous turn physics and checks only the final replay claims and completion.
The normal scripted interaction uses one proxy-button click per solution move in simplified mode and waits for the synchronous successful-turn count, not for autonomous task evolution.
The frozen definition requires autonomous non-clock task-state evolution to cause strict action-value loss, and explicitly excludes a static task whose opportunity remains actionable while waiting.
